open_points.subject: content-derived identities and content-addressed files
open_points.text: “Submitting content whose computed identity already exists returns the existing record unchanged” and “Equal bytes are stored once.” The texts do not say what happens when unequal content has the same SHA-256 digest.
open_points.question: How must the kernel handle a digest or generated-ID collision between unequal content?
options: Refuse the new content as a collision
Compare full content and use an additional identity mechanism
Treat the existing record or bytes as the submitted content
open_points.default_guess: Compare the full content and refuse on any unequal-content collision.

open_points.subject: A01/A05 ordering of edges and constants
open_points.text: Order-insensitive lists are sorted as “edges in the edge order of A05, constants by (`to_node`, `to_port`)”, but those keys tie for edges differing only in guards and for multiple constants targeting the same port.
open_points.question: What deterministic tie-breaker selects the first checked item and canonical list order when the stated sort keys are equal?
options: Use canonical JSON of the whole edge or constant as a final tie-breaker
Preserve request order for tied items
Reject tied sort keys during composition before proof
open_points.default_guess: Use canonical JSON of the complete item as a final tie-breaker, while retaining the later fan-in refusal.

open_points.subject: FlowNode.node_id and flow endpoints
open_points.text: “A flow input or flow output endpoint has the empty string as its node,” while no rule forbids a flow node whose `node_id` is the empty string.
open_points.question: May a node have an empty `node_id`, and if so how is it distinguished from a flow endpoint?
options: Refuse an empty node ID at composition
Represent endpoint kinds separately so an empty node ID remains legal
open_points.default_guess: Refuse an empty node ID at composition.

open_points.subject: flow and binding port schemas
open_points.text: M01 says `value_schema` is “written in the subset of JSON Schema the kernel supports”; A02 explicitly checks that for contract ports, but A05 gives no corresponding composition check and A08 only ambiguously imports selected A02 port rules.
open_points.question: Where, in what order, and with what outcome are unsupported schemas on flow ports, constants, and binding ports rejected?
options: Refuse composition or proposal before storing anything
Keep the object and make flow proof fail
Allow any schema outside contract ports
open_points.default_guess: Refuse the composition or binding proposal before persistence, using a fixed port-name order.

open_points.subject: TrialCase inputs and expected_outputs
open_points.text: A04 requires that “its input values fit the contract version's input ports” and that “its expected outputs, when present, fit the output ports,” but does not say whether missing or extra port entries are permitted or whether expected outputs may be partial.
open_points.question: Must trial inputs name exactly every input port, and when `expected_outputs` is present must it name exactly every output port?
options: Both maps must be exact
Inputs are exact but expected outputs may be partial
Missing entries are allowed and only supplied entries are checked
open_points.default_guess: Require exact inputs and, when expected outputs are present, exact outputs.

open_points.subject: sandbox filesystem access
open_points.text: K-02 says a function has “no filesystem beyond its input,” while A03 permits opening paths inside “the exchange directory and the read-only runtime.”
open_points.question: Which filesystem paths may agent code itself open, read, create or modify, as distinct from paths used internally by the runner and import machinery?
options: Agent code may access the runtime and exchange directory
Agent code may read runtime files but access only staged input/output paths in the exchange directory
All explicit file access by agent code is trapped
open_points.default_guess: Allow runtime access needed for imports, but restrict agent code's exchange-directory access to runner-defined input and output paths.

open_points.subject: sandbox input dictionary
open_points.text: An implementation receives “a dict with one entry per input port,” but the insertion order of that Python dict is not defined even though Python code can observe it.
open_points.question: In what order are input-port entries inserted into the dict passed to `run`?
options: Unicode code-point order of port name
The contract request's original port order
An unspecified order that functions must not rely on
open_points.default_guess: Insert entries in Unicode code-point order of port name.

open_points.subject: sandbox stdout and stderr
open_points.text: “Nothing the code prints or raises is interpreted by the kernel” and stdout is never kept, but the texts do not define whether stdout and stderr are discarded, drained, bounded, or allowed to block.
open_points.question: What happens when function code writes unbounded stdout or stderr, and can those writes cause timeout or resource exhaustion?
options: Connect both streams to a nonblocking discard sink
Drain both streams under a separate fixed byte ceiling
Let ordinary pipe behavior apply
open_points.default_guess: Send stdout and stderr directly to a discard sink so they neither accumulate nor block.

open_points.subject: ResourceBounds.process_count
open_points.text: Processes are limited with `setrlimit`, but `process_count` is not defined as counting children, the main interpreter, threads/tasks, or host processes sharing the UID.
open_points.question: Exactly what population is counted against `process_count`, and does the sandbox's initial interpreter count?
options: All sandbox tasks including the initial interpreter and threads
Only child processes created by the implementation
Only processes visible in the new PID namespace, excluding the runner
open_points.default_guess: Count every task in the sandbox PID namespace, including the initial interpreter.

open_points.subject: sandbox cleanup failure
open_points.text: If cleanup cannot be confirmed, “the execution is recorded `crashed` with detail `cleanup_failed`, and the kernel process stops,” but the disposition of the active surface request is not stated.
open_points.question: After recording `cleanup_failed`, does the kernel return the recorded failure, return `internal_error`, or terminate the connection before any response?
options: Return the recorded crashed execution and then stop
Return `internal_error` and then stop
Stop immediately without a response
open_points.default_guess: Persist the crashed record, return a bounded failure response if possible, then stop.

open_points.subject: release ceilings across upgrades
open_points.text: A20 says changed ceilings “bind contract versions issued after” a release, but most ceilings are not contract fields, and A13 derives mapped-list failure later from the current `stored_value_bytes_max`.
open_points.question: Which release's non-contract ceilings govern existing flow versions, runs resumed after upgrade, startup recovery, and later derivation of an already recorded mapped output list?
options: The release that created the contract or flow
The release under which the run started
The currently running release
open_points.default_guess: Pin all execution-relevant ceilings when the run starts and use that snapshot for recovery and trace derivation.

open_points.subject: store record order
open_points.text: K-17 gives records “one order,” while several store calls create or update multiple records in one transaction, but no within-transaction order or rule for updates is defined.
open_points.question: What is the total store order of records created together, and does updating a mutable record change its position?
options: Each operation defines a fixed insertion sequence and updates retain original position
All records in one transaction share a position with a secondary type order
Database insertion behavior determines the order
open_points.default_guess: Give each newly created record a unique sequence in a fixed operation-specific insertion order; updates retain their original position.

open_points.subject: empty many file values
open_points.text: A13 says an empty file list is named with its class, while M23 can name file inputs and outputs only through SpooledFile facts, of which an empty list has none.
open_points.question: What durable reference represents an empty `many` file value, its order, and its disclosure class in NodeExecution records and after restart?
options: Add a port-level file-list reference carrying class and an empty member list
Derive it solely from the flow graph and producing execution inputs
Represent an empty file list as a StoredValue
open_points.default_guess: Use an explicit port-level file-list reference carrying its class and ordered member references, including an empty list.

open_points.subject: manifest_revision
open_points.text: The manifest is read “at the configured `manifest_revision`,” but the texts do not define how a revision is resolved, verified, or read without changing the working tree.
open_points.question: What exact mechanism reads `<manifest_location>/<service_id>.json` at `manifest_revision`, and what revisions are valid?
options: Read a Git blob at an immutable commit ID
Require `manifest_location` to be an immutable revision directory
Read the current filesystem and use the revision only as metadata
open_points.default_guess: Require an immutable Git commit ID and read the file directly from that commit without modifying a checkout.

open_points.subject: ManifestOperation parsing
open_points.text: A08 rule 5 names some absent and invalid manifest fields but is silent on wrong JSON types and missing or malformed nested fields such as capability `name`, `exposed_as`, `effect_class`, `idempotency_key`, instances and required-header containers.
open_points.question: Which complete manifest shapes are accepted, and what deterministic check order applies to every missing, mistyped or malformed nested field?
options: Validate against a closed manifest schema before the listed semantic checks
Treat each malformed nested field as the corresponding listed manifest mismatch
Allow unmentioned shapes and let later code fail
open_points.default_guess: Validate against a closed manifest schema first, with a fixed field order, and report malformed structure as manifest mismatch.

open_points.subject: api_base_url
open_points.text: A08 accepts an absolute `http` or `https` URL with a host, and A09 forms the request by removing a trailing slash and appending the operation path; user information, query, fragment and an existing base path are not addressed.
open_points.question: Which URL components may `api_base_url` contain, and how are base paths, user information, queries and fragments handled?
options: Allow only scheme, host, optional port and optional path; forbid user information, query and fragment
Require origin-only URLs with no path
Permit all absolute URLs and apply literal concatenation
open_points.default_guess: Forbid user information, query and fragment; allow an explicit base path and concatenate it exactly as specified.

open_points.subject: plain HTTP loopback exception
open_points.text: Plain HTTP is allowed when the `api_base_url` “host is a loopback address,” but the text does not say whether this means a literal address, a DNS name resolving to loopback, IPv4-mapped IPv6, or every resolved address.
open_points.question: How is the loopback exception determined and protected against DNS changes between checking and connecting?
options: Only literal loopback IP addresses qualify
A hostname qualifies only when every resolved address is loopback and the connection is pinned to one of them
Any hostname currently resolving to a loopback address qualifies
open_points.default_guess: Allow only literal IPv4 or IPv6 loopback addresses.

open_points.subject: multipart port names
open_points.text: Multipart headers interpolate port names as `name="<port>"` and `filename="<port>"`, but port names have no stated character restriction or escaping rule.
open_points.question: How are quotes, backslashes, CR/LF, non-ASCII characters and other special characters in multipart port names handled?
options: Restrict port names to a safe ASCII field-name grammar
Escape them with one specified Content-Disposition encoding
Refuse only names that cannot be serialized safely
open_points.default_guess: Restrict all port names used in HTTP request construction to a safe ASCII identifier grammar.

open_points.subject: HTTP response Content-Encoding
open_points.text: The kernel sends `Accept-Encoding: identity`, but no rule says what happens if a service nevertheless returns a non-identity `Content-Encoding`.
open_points.question: Does the kernel decode, reject, or treat as raw bytes a response carrying a non-identity content encoding, and which bytes count toward the response ceiling?
options: Reject it as a malformed or contract-violating response
Decode supported encodings and count decoded bytes
Treat encoded bytes as the response body
open_points.default_guess: Reject any non-identity content encoding; for a 2xx response classify it as `contract_violation`.

open_points.subject: HTTP failure after final response headers
open_points.text: A09 classifies reset, EOF and timeout as “no valid final response received,” but also classifies outcomes by 2xx, 4xx and 5xx status; it does not settle a reset, timeout or malformed transfer body after a valid final status and headers arrived.
open_points.question: Which row wins when a valid final status was received but the response body or transfer framing did not complete?
options: The no-valid-response row always wins
The received status row wins, with an incomplete 2xx body treated as invalid output
The status row wins only when no outputs or body are required
open_points.default_guess: Use the received status row; treat an incomplete 2xx body as `contract_violation` and an applied non-read attempt.

open_points.subject: HTTP send certainty
open_points.text: “Nothing could be sent” holds only before “the kernel wrote the first byte of the request,” but the text does not define what to do when the HTTP/TLS library cannot prove whether application bytes reached the socket or peer.
open_points.question: What classification applies when the transport cannot establish whether the first request byte was written?
options: Conservatively use the may-have-been-sent outcome
Treat a client-reported connect failure as not sent
Require a transport adapter that reports this boundary exactly
open_points.default_guess: Conservatively classify any uncertainty as may-have-been-sent.

open_points.subject: token-list configuration reload
open_points.text: A16 re-reads when bytes differ or the file cannot be read, and after a failed re-read refuses every request “until a re-read passes.” If the file is restored to the exact previous valid bytes, its digest no longer differs from the last successful read.
open_points.question: After any failed re-read, does the kernel retry a full parse on every request even when the restored bytes equal the last successful configuration?
options: Retry every request until one full re-read succeeds
Resume using the old list when the old byte digest reappears
Remain unavailable until the file changes to a new digest
open_points.default_guess: Retry a full re-read on every request while configuration is in the failed state.

open_points.subject: token format and minimum length
open_points.text: Tokens must be “at least 43 characters (32 bytes in base64url),” but the rules do not require base64url syntax or say whether length means Unicode code points, UTF-8 bytes or decoded bytes.
open_points.question: What token alphabet and length calculation are required at startup and reload?
options: Require unpadded base64url decoding to at least 32 bytes
Accept any Unicode string of at least 43 code points
Accept any UTF-8 string of at least 43 bytes
open_points.default_guess: Require ASCII unpadded base64url that decodes to at least 32 bytes.

open_points.subject: credential-header collision startup check
open_points.text: A09 says a credential header colliding with a required or kernel-set header “refuses to start,” but the startup rules do not say which manifest records are read or what happens if those records or selected instances are missing or malformed.
open_points.question: What manifest and instance validation is performed at startup solely to check credential-header collisions, and does an unavailable or malformed manifest stop the whole kernel?
options: Validate every configured service and stop on any unreadable manifest
Check collisions only for manifest entries that can be read, deferring other failures to invocation
Do no manifest work at startup and report collisions per service request
open_points.default_guess: Read selected instances at startup for collision checks, but defer unrelated manifest defects to proposal or invocation unless the collision check itself cannot be performed safely.

open_points.subject: redacted failure_detail length
open_points.text: A07 says a protected `failure_detail` is returned to an agent “only as its length and that class,” without defining the length unit.
open_points.question: Is the disclosed length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode scalar values, grapheme clusters, or the pre-truncation text?
options: UTF-8 bytes of the stored truncated detail
Unicode code points of the stored detail
Original body or exception length before truncation
open_points.default_guess: Return the UTF-8 byte length of the stored, already truncated failure detail.
